lesson_scope: Equilibrium of particles on rough inclined planes; complete range of values of an applied force (parallel, horizontal, or at an angle) maintaining static equilibrium; dual limiting equilibrium thresholds (downward slip vs upward slip); angle of repose considerations; connected particles across crest pulleys with hanging counterweights; and double-inclined symmetrical rough wedges.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Basic range for force parallel to rough slope

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Basic range for force parallel to rough slope

hints: Downhill gravity is $W_\parallel = 50\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$, and normal reaction is $R = 50\cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$, giving $F_{\max} = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$.
At lower limit (slipping down), friction acts up: $P_{\min} = 25 - 8.66 = 16.3\text{ N}$. At upper limit (slipping up), friction acts down: $P_{\max} = 25 + 8.66 = 33.7\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate normal reaction and maximum static friction:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 50\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3013\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\max} = \mu R = 0.2(25\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.6603\text{ N}$$

Calculate the dual limiting equilibrium thresholds along the slope:
- Lower limit (on the point of slipping down):
$$P_{\min} = mg\sin 30^\circ - F_{\max} = 25 - 5\sqrt{3} \approx 16.3397 \approx 16.3\text{ N}$$
- Upper limit (on the point of slipping up):
$$P_{\max} = mg\sin 30^\circ + F_{\max} = 25 + 5\sqrt{3} \approx 33.6603 \approx 33.7\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Range: } 16.3\text{ N} \leqslant P \leqslant 33.7\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the baseline forces:
- Downhill pull of gravity is $25\text{ N}$.
- Maximum friction resistance is:
$$F_{\max} = 0.2(50\cos 30^\circ) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$$

Find the range of holding forces:
- To stop downward slide: $P \geqslant 25 - 8.66 = 16.3\text{ N}$.
- To avoid dragging upward: $P \leqslant 25 + 8.66 = 33.7\text{ N}$:
$$16.3\text{ N} \leqslant P \leqslant 33.7\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates normal reaction $R = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ and maximum friction $F_{\max} = 0.2(25\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$.

$$\tan 20^\circ \approx 0.36397 < \mu = 0.5$$

$$F_{\max} = 0.5(40\cos 20^\circ) \approx 18.7939\text{ N}$$
Since $W_\parallel < F_{\max}$, the block does not slide under its own weight, so equilibrium holds when $P = 0$.

Calculate the maximum pulling force $P_{\max}$ up the slope:
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = P_{\max} - W_\parallel - F_{\max} = 0$$
$$P_{\max} = 13.6808 + 18.7939 = 32.4747 \approx 32.5\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Range for non-negative pull: } 0 \leqslant P \leqslant 32.5\text{ N}$$

- Slope is gentle ($\tan 20^\circ \approx 0.364$), while friction is strong ($\mu = 0.5$):
$$W_\parallel < F_{\max} \implies 13.68\text{ N} < 18.79\text{ N}$$
The block stays parked on the slope even when no force is applied ($P = 0$).

Find upper pulling limit:
- Overcoming gravity and friction requires:
$$P_{\max} = 13.68 + 18.79 = 32.5\text{ N}$$
Pulling with any force up to $32.5\text{ N}$ maintains equilibrium.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Identifying actual friction force and direction for intermediate applied load

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Identifying actual friction force and direction for intermediate applied load

hints: Downhill gravity is $100\sin 30^\circ = 50\text{ N}$. The applied pull $P = 60\text{ N}$ is larger than gravity, so the parcel tends to slip up the slope.
Friction opposes the upward tendency by acting down the slope. By equilibrium along the slope: $60 - 50 - F_f = 0 \implies F_f = 10\text{ N}$ down the slope.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the net tendency of motion along the slope:
- Downhill component of weight: $W_\parallel = 100\sin 30^\circ = 50\text{ N}$.
- Uphill applied pull: $P = 60\text{ N}$.
Since $60\text{ N} > 50\text{ N}$, the tendency is to slip up the slope, so friction must act down the slope:
$$F_\text{tendency} = 60 - 50 = 10\text{ N} \quad (\text{uphill})$$

Calculate the actual friction force and check against the maximum threshold:
$$F_f = P - W_\parallel = 60 - 50 = 10\text{ N} \quad (\text{acting down the slope})$$
Note that $F_{\max} = \mu mg\cos 30^\circ = 0.4(50\sqrt{3}) = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$. Since $10\text{ N} < 34.6\text{ N}$, the parcel remains stationary with:
$$F_f = 10\text{ N} \quad (\text{down the slope})$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compare the competing forces:
- Uphill pull is $60\text{ N}$.
- Downhill gravity is $50\text{ N}$:
$$P > W_\parallel \implies 60\text{ N} > 50\text{ N}$$
The pull wins, so the parcel tries to creep upwards.

Determine actual friction:
- Friction resists by pointing downhill with exactly the required balancing force:
$$F_f = 60 - 50 = 10\text{ N} \quad (\text{down the slope})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Compares upward pull $60\text{ N}$ with downhill gravity $100\sin 30^\circ = 50\text{ N}$ to establish upward slip tendency (friction acts down).
Calculates $F_f = 60 - 50 = 10\text{ N}$ acting down the slope (confirming $10\text{ N} < F_{\max} = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 6: Range of horizontal pushing force on rough incline

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Range of horizontal pushing force on rough incline

hints: Perpendicular to the slope: $R = 50\cos 45^\circ + P\sin 45^\circ = \frac{50 + P}{\sqrt{2}}$. Along slope: $P\cos 45^\circ \pm 0.2 R = 50\sin 45^\circ \implies P \pm 0.2(50 + P) = 50$.
For $P_{\min}$ (friction up): $1.2P = 40 \implies P_{\min} = \frac{100}{3} \approx 33.3\text{ N}$. For $P_{\max}$ (friction down): $0.8P = 60 \implies P_{\max} = 75\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express normal reaction perpendicular to the incline:
$$R = mg\cos 45^\circ + P\sin 45^\circ = \frac{50 + P}{\sqrt{2}}$$

Solve for the dual horizontal limits along the slope:
- Downward slip limit (friction up):
$$\frac{P}{\sqrt{2}} + 0.2\left(\frac{50 + P}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \frac{50}{\sqrt{2}} \implies 1.2P = 40 \implies P_{\min} = \frac{100}{3} \approx 33.3\text{ N}$$
- Upward slip limit (friction down):
$$\frac{P}{\sqrt{2}} - 0.2\left(\frac{50 + P}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \frac{50}{\sqrt{2}} \implies 0.8P = 60 \implies P_{\max} = \frac{60}{0.8} = 75\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Range: } 33.3\text{ N} \leqslant P \leqslant 75\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Form the governing horizontal equation:
- After canceling the $1/\sqrt{2}$ geometric factor from the $45^\circ$ angle:
$$P \pm 0.2(50 + P) = 50$$

Compute the push interval:
- Minimum push to prevent falling: $1.2P = 40 \implies P_{\min} = 33.3\text{ N}$.
- Maximum push before sliding up: $0.8P = 60 \implies P_{\max} = 75\text{ N}$:
$$33.3\text{ N} \leqslant P \leqslant 75\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses normal reaction $R = \frac{50 + P}{\sqrt{2}}$ and writes parallel equilibrium: $P \pm 0.2(50 + P) = 50$.
Evaluates $P_{\min} = \frac{40}{1.2} = \frac{100}{3} \approx 33.3\text{ N}$ and $P_{\max} = \frac{60}{0.8} = 75\text{ N}$.
